Previous radiance field representations lack a concrete definition for surface geometry, resulting in bumpy surfaces; SDFs resolve this by providing an implicit surface definition [S6].

The claim states that previous radiance field representations lack a concrete definition for surface geometry, resulting in bumpy surfaces, and that SDFs resolve this by providing an implicit surface definition. Source [S6] explicitly contains the sentence: 'Prior works on 3D GANs have typically represented the geometry as a radiance field [38], which lacks a concrete definition for where the surface geometry resides in the field, resulting in bumpy surfaces. A number of works [44, 62, 71] have proposed alternate representations based on implicit surfaces (such as signed distance functions, or SDFs) that can be used with neural volume rendering.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
